title: Proposal Writing — Win Story
subtitle: You send detailed, professional proposals that prospects read, compliment, and then go
useWhen: silent on.Your proposals are comprehensive but they don't compel action. They document your solution but don't tell a story.
howToUse: A Win Story is a proposal structure that mirrors how humans make decisions - through narrative, not specifications. The structure has six parts: Situation (their world as it is today), Complication (the problem and its cost), Resolution (what success looks like), Solution (your approach- positioned as the bridge from complication to resolution), Proof (evidence that you can deliver), and Call to Action (one clear, specific next step). The key difference from a standard proposal is that the customer's story comes first. Your solution is a supporting character, not the lead.
steps: Write the Situation and Complication sections using the prospect's exact words from your discovery call.
The Resolution section should describe their future state not your features.
Proof should be a specific result, not a general claim.

The Call to Action must be one thing not a list of next steps. Write proposals that close, not just inform Proof Needs a Match Generic proof is worse than none. If your Proof example doesn't mirror the Complication you named earlier, the reader notices the gap and starts doubting the rest of the proposal instead of trusting it.
origin: Solution selling methodology — Win Story narrative structure
promptBody:
Act as a proposal writing consultant using the Win Story structure.
Discovery call notes   :    [PASTE KEY POINTS FROM YOUR CALL]
My solution                  :    [WHAT YOU ARE PROPOSING TO DO]
Proof available             :    [CASE STUDY, DATA, OR REFERENCE]
Desired next step        :    [WHAT YOU WANT THEM TO DO NEXT]
Write a complete Win Story proposal:
SITUATION             :   Their world as it is today their terms
COMPLICATION    :   The problem and the cost of it continuing
RESOLUTION         :   What their world looks like when solved
SOLUTION              :   Your approach bridge to the resolution
PROOF                     :   One specific result that proves delivery
CALL TO ACTION  :   One sentence, one next step, one date

proTip:
The single most impactful change to any proposal: move the executive summary to after
the Complication section, not at the top. Prospects who feel their problem has been
understood read proposals differently. Understanding before solution is the sequence
that closes.
